key_insight: LizTail lets a fixed systolic array adapt both its shape and its parallel execution layout by splitting the array into reconfigurable segments with only endpoint connectivity.
engineering_relevance: This improves utilization on irregular workloads like skinny CNN matrices and small-batch LLM decoding, where conventional fixed arrays waste compute and underuse available parallelism.
method: Partition a 128×128 array into 32 regular 128×4 segments.
Add only predefined endpoint links for trimming, turn-back extension, and distributed execution.
Use a hardware-constrained mapper to choose execution organization, dataflow, partitioning, and tiling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports geometric-mean speedups of 5.02× for CNN inference and 25.67× for LLM decoding over a TPU-like array, with EDP reductions up to 38.23×.
watch_item: The design depends on segmented reconfiguration and specialized buffers/control, so real hardware may face routing, timing, and implementation complexity tradeoffs.
paper_title: LizTail: Unifying Shape Adaptation and Spatial Parallelism with Segment-Reconfigurable Systolic Arrays
